about: The API side of the 27 Oct overnight work: surrogate bids, withdraw and price cap through spine.ai's API path (GET /api/run-case-api — no browser; the API planner writes the calls from the sentence). Each case says what should happen; 'to confirm' marks an expectation nobody has checked against Procol's rules yet.

cases.text: Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it and place a surrogate bid of 100 for that vendor.
Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 2 vendors, publish it and place a surrogate bid of 100 for one vendor and 120 for the other.
Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it and try to place a surrogate bid of -50 for that vendor; it should be refused.
Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it and try to place a surrogate bid with no price for that vendor; it should be refused.
Create a technical-only event with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it and submit a surrogate technical response for that vendor.
Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it, then withdraw the event with a remark and check its status is withdrawn.
Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it, place a surrogate bid for that vendor, then withdraw the event with a remark and check its status is withdrawn.
Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it, then try to withdraw the event without any remark; it should be refused (to confirm).
Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it, withdraw the event with a remark, then try to place a surrogate bid for that vendor; it should be refused.
Create an auction with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it, then withdraw the event with a remark and check its status is withdrawn.
Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it and set a price cap of 100 for that vendor.

Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it, set a price cap of 100 for that vendor, then place a surrogate bid of 120 for that vendor; it should be refused because it is above the cap.
Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it, set a price cap of 100 for that vendor, then place a surrogate bid of 90 for that vendor.

Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor, publish it, set a price cap of 100 for that vendor, then place a surrogate bid of 100 for that vendor (equal to the cap); it should be refused because a bid must be below the cap.
